content.thinking:
I need to plan out realistic monster truck proportions in one pass without iterative testing—big tires around 1.68m diameter, overall length near 5.5m, width around 3.6m, height about 3.4m, with the body mounted above the chassis and wheel axles positioned accordingly.

For the wheels, I'm working out how to orient cylindrical tires along the X-axis using the part/lathe helper functions, then building tread lugs as boxes arranged radially around the tire and merging them into one geometry using transform matrices in the wheel's local coordinate frame.

Adding center cap and bolt details... Now placing wheels at front/rear z positions, setting axle height so the tire touches ground, and arranging 16 tread lugs radially around the tire so one lines up at the bottom contact point.

I'm working through the rotation math to make sure the wheel's local axes align correctly with world space after rotating the cylinder to face the right direction, relying on the 16-lug symmetry so any 90°-multiple roll keeps the bottom lug flush with the ground.

For the lugs themselves, I'm placing 16 boxes radially around the tire core at roughly 0.79 units out, each rotated to align its radial axis, sized to extend the tread to about 0.84 total radius for a chunky look. I'm considering whether to add extra sidewall details like small lugs or lettering rings but may skip that for simplicity.

For the sidewall painting I'll use cellPaint logic keyed off axis orientation: sidewalls get radial ring stripes computed from distance to the wheel's center, with a grey-black band, a white/red accent stripe, and dark fill elsewhere plus some speckled noise, while the tread gets dithered noise texture.

Lugs get colored with the same cellPaint approach since merged parts can still accept paint based on world positions even without proper UVs. For the chassis I'm laying out ladder frame boxes spanning the body length, adding axle rods connecting wheels at ride height, a differential housing sphere at center, four-link suspension bars from axle to frame, and coilover shocks at each corner.

Now I'm positioning the shocks carefully so they clear the tire inner faces, placing springs as cylinders with coil-like stripe patterns via cellPaint, then adjusting shock endpoints to run from the axle up to the frame mounts. For the body, I'm defining the truck shell sections: hood up front, cab in the middle, and bed toward the rear, each spanning specific z-ranges along the frame.

I'm checking that the body width sits inside the wheel inner faces so the tires don't overlap the shell, and that the body bottom sits above the tire tops so the wheels read as separate elements beside the frame. For the body surface itself, I want to use a procedural paint function to render a red-orange gradient with flame graphics licking up the lower sides, driven by a noise-based height function along the vertical axis.

For the flames themselves, I'm defining a zigzag/triangle-wave pattern to shape the fire tips along the car's length, layering yellow and orange bands over a deep blue base body color for a classic hot-rod flame look. Now I'm laying out the hood as a box roughly 1.9 units wide and 0.7 tall, centered appropriately along the car's length.

Continuing the cab structure: lower box for the cab, narrower greenhouse box on top, with window decals as simple pixel-art textured planes applied to the front, back, and side faces rather than full glass modeling.

I'm designing the truck bed as an open structure with floor, side walls, and tailgate, adding a roll cage and light bar inside rather than fenders since the body sits between the oversized wheels. For the front end, I'm building a dark steel bumper with chrome trim, a grille texture, and glowing headlight boxes.

Now I'm working on the hood details: a scoop with a dark intake, a racing stripe decal down the center, and pixel-art number decals reading "88" on the doors using a simple glyph grid pattern.

I'm sizing the plate texture with a texel of 0.04 so it lines up with the body paint's pixel cells, and placing it just outside the lower cab box near the door at roughly y=1.9. I'm also starting to think about adding sponsor decals as further embellishment.

Rather than a text-based sponsor logo, I'm considering a pixel-art skull emblem placed on top of the hood, which means rotating that plane -90° about the X axis so it faces upward correctly, working through the rotation math to make sure the texture's orientation stays upright once flattened onto the hood surface.

I'll stick with the dir-based approach consistently for all planes, including the back-facing one, since it avoids needing extra mirroring logic. For texel density, I'm calculating that the paint sheet resolution should be fine at a 0.05 cell size given the model's surface area, so I'll keep the default 1024 texture but adjust the body cell size accordingly.

For the remaining details, I'm planning out a roof-mounted light bar with six glowing boxes, dual vertical chrome exhaust stacks behind the cab with angled caps and small glowing tips to suggest flame, side mirrors as simple boxes near the cab, thin dark door seam lines with small chrome handle boxes, and I'm about to add side steps.

I'm continuing with rock sliders as dark boxes under the cab, visible frame rails and crossmembers, a driveshaft running along the centerline with differential spheres at the axles, steering rods, a front winch with hook, an underbody skid plate, glowing red taillights on the bed with a license plate decal, a ridged tailgate, lug nuts on the wheels, and I'm now working out how to represent the coilover springs and shock bodies using stacked cylinder geometry.

Painting the coil bands using a periodic rule based on height, alternating yellow and dark yellow stripes to suggest spring coils, then adding a thin antenna rod with a small red flag box on the bed corner, and applying a mud-spatter dither to the lower body panels using the noise function to vary the brown tones. I'm also keeping the flat color palette under 64 entries while setting up the final metadata and imports for the build script.

I'm sketching out the builder setup now, importing geometry utilities and a glow wrapper, then defining a helper function that creates boxed parts with position and color, wrapping each in the glow/part system so I can call it repeatedly for the truck's components.

Now I'm writing the body paint logic, using noise-based mud splatter along the lower band of the body and adding racing stripes centered on the x-axis for the upper portion.

For the flame decal, I'm computing a triangle-wave tip height along z to create a jagged flame silhouette, then coloring regions below the tip yellow near the bottom, orange in the middle, and red near the tip, restricted to side and front surfaces so the hood top stays clean.

Writing tire sidewall paint logic...

I'm keeping the sidewall flat rather than adding a shoulder, and working out wheel placement: narrowing track width to a more realistic 2.9m by setting wheel centers at ±1.45 with 0.95 tyre width, then checking clearance between the body (±0.9) and shocks so the tyre doesn't overlap the frame near the top.

Now I'm positioning the shocks and frame rails so they clear the body - frame at x±0.45, shock mounts around x±0.7-0.75 - but realizing the shocks would be hidden inside the body if placed there, so I'm considering raising the body floor and mounting visible suspension towers between the body and tyres instead.

Setting body bottom at y=1.85 with cab from 1.85-2.55, greenhouse to 3.3, roof to 3.38, hood 1.85-2.45, keeping the 1.68 tyre-top clearance so the body doesn't overlap the tyres in x. Total height comes to about 3.4-3.55 with the light bar, which feels close to real-world monster truck proportions (~3.7), so this seems like a reasonable layout.

Now I'm working out the frame underneath: rails at x±0.45 running y1.25-1.55 for the full z-length, with crossmembers, orange body-mount posts bridging 1.55-1.85, and a dark underbody floor pan filling the gap between frame and body. I'm also placing shock tower mounts as boxes near x±0.7 spanning roughly y1.4-1.8.

For the suspension, I'm giving each wheel a V-shaped pair of shocks — a lower mount near the axle at (±0.85, 0.95, z) and upper mounts splayed slightly fore and aft at (±0.7, 1.8, z±0.3) — approximating one per wheel position at the front and rear axle z-locations.

Now I'm detailing the shocks: a thin red rod body with a yellow-banded spring cylinder wrapped around it, oriented along the direction between the two mount points, with the bands painted using a modulo pattern on world y-coordinate for alternating stripes. Then I'm adding the axles as grey rods spanning the width at the wheel height, connecting the inner tire faces across the car.

Still placing axle components... I'm positioning portal gearbox boxes near each wheel hub inside the tire cavity, a differential housing box at the centre, four-link suspension rods connecting the axles to the frame at angled points, and a driveshaft rod running front-to-back at hub height.

Now I'm adding steering tie rods across the front axle, a skid plate box beneath the frame, and front-end details like a bumper, hood section, grille texture plane, and glowing headlight boxes positioned near the nose of the body.

For the scoop front, I'll place a dark intake plane with a pixel-art grille pattern of slats reusing the palette style. Now I'm figuring out the windshield and greenhouse geometry, aligning the hood's rear edge with where the cab's lower body and glass should begin.

Placing side and rear window planes, then designing a pixel-art window texture generator with dark gradient bands and diagonal light streaks, scaling texel density based on window dimensions (roughly 0.05 units per pixel).

Windows are inset smaller than the greenhouse cutout so painted body color shows as a frame, and I'm skipping flame paint there since the tip stays below threshold. Now adding cab door details—vertical seam lines and plate numbering positioned along the lower body.

Adding more body details...

Reconsidering placement, I decide to position the exhaust stacks outside the cab corners near the rear, checking clearance against the tire positions so they don't clip, and settling on x ±1.0, z ≈ -0.88 hugging the cab's rear corner.

Now I'm laying out the truck bed: floor, side walls, and tailgate as boxes with painted surfaces, plus a decal stripe on the tailgate, glowing red tail light boxes at the rear corners, and a ribbed dark mat for the bed floor interior.

For the bed liner I'm using a small tiled pattern for a ribbed texture effect. Then I'm adding a roll bar made of simple rigid rods instead of a single polyline sweep -- two vertical posts, a top crossbar, and brace rods -- positioned toward the back of the bed for stability and visual simplicity.

Adding light pods on the roll bar, a thin antenna rod with a small flag box at the top, and then working out wheel hub geometry -- a rim disc sized to sit centered within the tire's outer face at each wheel position.

Computing lug nut and beadlock bolt positions...

Placing 16 lugs at 22.5° increments around the wheel in world space, checking that the radial spacing creates good tread gaps with the core cylinder, then considering staggered shoulder blocks for extra tread detail.

I'm checking that Row A sits flat on the floor exactly, within tolerance, and confirming the lug counts: 16+32 per wheel ×4 wheels gives 192 boxes merging into 4 parts, roughly 2300 triangles per wheel, which is efficient. Now I'm setting up the tyre core cylinder geometry and verifying the painted merged geometry looks right.

Next I'm working out sidewall coverage against the rim and lugs, and adding a dithered mud layer near the bottom of the tyre using noise to blend brown mud into the tread. Then I'm defining the blue color palette for the vehicle.

Adding more colors...

Still working out the skull decal pixel grid...

Using white "#f2f2ee" and black "#14141a" for the skull colors, and switching the racing stripe to navy with white edges so the skull has good contrast against it instead of blending into white. Placing the skull decal on the hood near the stripe at a small offset to avoid z-fighting, then moving on to designing the door number plates.

For the door plates, I'm working out a 13x9 pixel grid for a two-digit number like "8", sizing glyphs at 5px wide with proper margins so the digits don't touch the plate border, and considering an orange ring around a white plate background to frame the numbers clearly.

Checking plate sizing (0.65x0.45) against the door opening and cab dimensions to make sure it fits within the body panel without overlapping the flame decals below. Then I'm adding a checkered race-flag strip texture for the tailgate as another decal element.

Next I'm sizing a small license plate for the tailgate using a simple blue-and-white pixel pattern, then adding a rear bumper bar with a tow hook, while deciding to skip fender flares and front hood numbering for now.

I'm positioning dark rock sliders along the cab sides between the frame rails and body bottom, then working out an underbody pan box sized to the body footprint and spanning most of the vehicle's length.

Now I'm laying out orange frame posts, rails, and cross members with specific positions along the frame, plus small suspension tower boxes mounted near the rails to connect up to the shock mounts.

Working through the shock geometry, setting upper mounts around y1.6 under the towers and lower mounts near the axle at y0.95, checking the resulting spring length is reasonable, and then placing the axle and verifying the lower shock point sits just inside the tire's inner edge.

Checking front axle z-position and tire clearance against the hood and bumper—confirming no overlap since the tire sits outboard of the body width, and the bumper clears the tire top vertically. I'm deciding to skip mud flaps for now but noting I should add tow hooks, winch details, and a chrome headlight bezel for extra realism.

Now I'm working out positioning for turn indicators, hood latch pins, and vent lines, then checking whether the grille plane on the hood front overlaps with the headlights or bumper cover given their respective z and y coordinates—confirming the widths and heights line up without clashing.

I adjust the grille's centered y and height so it clears the bumper, align headlights to match, and note the flame paint falls below the grille on the hood's front face. Part count lands around 250, so I'm ready to move to code with a small helper function for creating colored box geometry at given positions.

Now I'm setting up decal and glow helper functions for planes and glowing parts, then starting to construct the wheel geometry with a cylinder core positioned by side and z offset.

Still writing wheel construction...

Skipping axle stubs and decal details, I'm finalizing rim and dish colors, then writing the body paint function with a triangle-wave helper and a luminance calculation based on surface normals for shading.

Adding mud splatter and stripe logic...

I realize the flame tip formula risks bleeding onto the hood top since its peak exceeds the hood's y-level, so I'm restricting flames to the side/front/back axes only and capping the tip height lower to stay clear of the greenhouse sides too.

For flame coloring I'm building a bottom-to-top ramp from red to orange to yellow based on how close each point is to the flame tip, using dithered picks between ramp colors, falling back to the blue stripe ramp elsewhere. Now I'm starting to think through how the bed liner's interior wall faces should be painted.

Adding chevron stripe decals...

For windows, I'm writing a pixel-texture function that shades panes darker at top and lighter toward the bottom, with diagonal light streaks for a glassy look.

Moving to the exhaust flame and antenna details, I'm using spike and rod helper functions to build glowing flame geometry and thin rods with flat caps for antennas, then continuing on to mirrors and the brush guard.

Laying out the brush guard verticals and top bar, adding a winch box with fairlead near the bumper, small hinge pins on the hood corners, rear tow hooks as red boxes, and a steering tie rod for the front axle.

Skipping brake rotors since they're hidden inside the tire. Setting the body-height variable and double-checking the color helper functions return the right types before finalizing the code.
